mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces discount rates, which raises the present value of expected corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and remains above for at least two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS reverts below 5% within 30 days, negating the policy persistence.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal, or UNRATE remains above 4% while PAYEMS does not show consistent growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% month-over-month accompanied by rising retail sales (implied via HOUST) indicates expanding economic activity, which anticipates higher corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite both proxies rising, or the increase in INDPRO is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL < 305 over three consecutive months) reduces the Fed's incentive to raise rates, lowering risk aversion and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 305 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or CPIAUCSL reaccelerates above 305 within 10 days, reversing the deflation signal.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for four consecutive months, the market anticipates lower policy tightening, which amplifies equity valuation multiples and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative, or FEDFUNDS reverts above 4% within 30 days, invalidating the low-rate expectation.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (implied by PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which elevates wage growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE remains < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or UNRATE begins to rise while PAYEMS remains elevated, breaking the tightness pattern.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and industrial production (INDPRO) suggest weakening demand, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 300 and INDPRO < INDPRO_prev for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or both proxies revert to growth in the following observation window.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-specific effect: in a deflationary regime (CPIAUCSL < 295 and FEDFUNDS > 5%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are more likely to be positive due to risk-off reversal, despite negative macro momentum.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 295 and FEDFUNDS > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in this regime (p > 0.05) or the regime definition is not met for the 20-day window.
